summary: The command palette (Ctrl+K, or ⌘+K on a Mac): a searchable list of pages, actions, scenario replays, open incidents and customers, ranked by a small fuzzy subsequence matcher and fully usable from the keyboard. It caches API data for 15 seconds and doubles as the API-key prompt when a write request is rejected outside demo mode. main.js installs it, passes in shared actions (open a drawer, toggle traffic) and calls `askForKey()` when api.js reports `auth:required`.

notes.text: File header: the command palette opens with Ctrl+K (⌘+K on a Mac) and lets you navigate, replay scenarios, toggle settings or jump straight to an incident or customer.
API helpers: `get` and `post` for data and scenario runs, and `setKey` to store an API key typed into the palette.
DOM helpers: `$` (a `querySelector` shortcut), the auto-escaping `html` template, `mount`, and `trapTab`, which keeps Tab inside the open palette.
Motion helpers: `animate`; `motionEnabled` and `setMotion` for the motion toggle command; `spring` and `stagger` for the opening and list animations.
The icon builder and the toast notifier.

Module-level state: `items` is every available command, `filtered` is what the current search shows, `selected` is the highlighted row's index, `mode` is 'commands' or 'key' (the API-key prompt), `onKey` is the callback to run once a key is saved, and `generation` counts openings so a late close can tell it is stale. `lastFocus` is the element that gets focus back when the palette closes.
A small cache of API data (incidents, customers, scenarios), with `at` recording when it was fetched.
`root()` returns the `#palette` container from index.html.
`paletteOpen()` is exported so main.js can handle Escape and the Ctrl+K toggle correctly.
Doc comment for the fuzzy matcher: the query's letters must appear in the text in order (a subsequence, so 'tgl' matches 'Toggle'), with bonus points for letters at the start of a word.
`score(text, query)` returns a number, higher for better matches. An empty query matches everything with the same score, 1.
Lower-cases the text, then sets up `s` (the running score) and `t` (the position where the search for the next letter starts).
For each query letter, finds its next occurrence at or after position `t`. If any letter is missing the item doesn't match at all, so the function returns 0.

Points for each letter: 3 if it sits exactly where the search resumed (right after the previous match, or at the very start of the text for the first letter), 2 if it follows a space (a word start), otherwise 1. The search is greedy: it always takes the earliest occurrence.
Moves the search position past the matched letter, which is what forces the letters to appear in order; then the loop closes.
The final score is the points plus the points divided by the text's length. The second term is a smaller tie-breaker that ranks a shorter, more specific text above a longer one with the same points.
Closes `score()`.
`loadData()` refreshes the cache, but skips the network entirely when the data is under 15 seconds old, so opening the palette repeatedly stays instant.
Fetches four lists in parallel: up to 40 open incidents, up to 20 under investigation, every customer and the scenario catalog.
Stores the results with a timestamp. Open and investigating incidents are merged into one list; resolved incidents are not offered.
Closes `loadData()`.

`build(actions)` turns everything into one flat list of palette items. `actions` is passed in from main.js (`openIncident`, `openUser`, `toggleTraffic`), which keeps page-specific code out of this file.
The eight pages, each written as `[route key, label, icon, hint]`. The hint shows the matching two-key shortcut: 'G O' means press g, then o (handled in main.js).
Turns each page into an item in the 'Go to' group whose `run` changes `location.hash`; the router in main.js reacts to that and renders the page.
The 'Actions' group starts with 'Toggle live traffic', which calls the shared action that starts or stops the demo event generator.
The motion toggle's label reflects the current state ('Reduce motion' or 'Enable motion'). Running it flips the setting and confirms the new state in a toast.
Opens FastAPI's interactive API documentation at `/docs` in a new tab; `noopener` isolates the new tab from this page.

'Reset demo data…' only navigates to the Simulation page, where the real reset button must be pressed and held. A destructive action therefore can't be fired by a stray Enter in the palette. The last line closes the list.
One 'Run scenario' item per scenario in the cache, with its category (attack, fraud…) as the hint. Its `run` is async because it calls the API.
Replays the scenario through the real backend pipeline with `POST /simulation/{key}`.

Shows a toast with the customer's name and the peak score and level, coloured by that level. If the run produced an incident, clicking the toast opens it; otherwise `onClick` is `undefined` and the toast simply dismisses.
Any failure, such as a rejected API key, becomes a red CRITICAL toast showing the server's message.
Closes `run`, the item object and the `map` call.
One item per open or investigating incident, labelled like 'INC-0001 · title' and hinted with severity and customer name; running it opens the incident drawer.
One item per customer, hinted with their ID and current risk score; running it opens the customer drawer.
Returns every item in display order: pages, actions, scenarios, incidents, customers. The last line closes `build()`.
`renderList(query)` redraws the visible results for the current search text into the `.palette-list` element.
Scores each item against one combined string of its label, hint and group name, so typing 'customers' lists every customer and typing an incident or customer ID finds that record.

Keeps only matches (score above 0) and sorts them best-first, but only while a query is typed: with an empty query the comparator returns 0, and because JavaScript's sort is stable the build order is kept. At most 40 results are shown.
Clamps `selected` so it still points at a real row after the list shrinks.
`group` remembers the last group header written, so a header is only printed when the group changes.
Mounts the results into the list (or, if there are none, the 'No matches' message on line 71).

Emits a group header whenever this item's group differs from the previous one. The assignment `(group = item.group)` inside the template both updates the tracker and prints the name; when results are sorted by score, groups can interleave, so a header may appear more than once.
Each result is a `button` with `role="option"`, its index in `data-i` and `aria-selected` marking the highlighted row. Inside are the icon, the label and an optional right-aligned hint.
Closes the mapping, falls back to 'No matches' when nothing matched, and closes `renderList()`.
`highlight()` moves the selection after an arrow-key press without re-rendering the list; it loops over the rows already on screen.
A row is selected when its `data-i` equals `selected`. Its `aria-selected` is set to 'true' or 'false' to match, which also drives the highlight style in CSS.
Scrolls the selected row into view only as far as needed (`block: "nearest"`), so the list doesn't jump around.
Closes the loop and `highlight()`.
`frame(placeholder)` returns the palette's markup. It starts with a backdrop that closes the palette when clicked (`data-close`).
The dialog box, marked as a modal dialog with an accessible name for screen readers.

The input row: a key icon in key mode or a search icon otherwise, then the text input with autocomplete and spellcheck turned off. In key mode the input also gets `type=password` so the pasted key is masked (that string has no special characters, so `html` inserts it unchanged); the 'esc' badge reminds users how to close.
The results container, with `role="listbox"` to match the `option` rows rendered inside it.
The footer: in key mode it explains that Enter saves the key for this browser session only (api.js keeps it in `sessionStorage`); otherwise it lists the keyboard controls.
Closes the dialog box, the template and `frame()`.
`show()` makes the palette visible.
Every opening bumps `generation`, so a close animation that began before this opening knows not to hide it.
When the palette opens from hidden, remembers the element that had focus, so `closePalette()` can give it back.
Unhides the overlay.
Fades the backdrop in over 200ms.
Pops the box in: it fades in, grows from 96% and drops 10px into place with a spring ease.
Puts the cursor in the input so the user can start typing immediately; closes `show()`.
`openPalette(actions)` opens the command list. If the palette is already open, the same shortcut closes it instead, making Ctrl+K a toggle.
Switches to command mode, mounts a fresh frame with the search placeholder and shows it.
Builds and renders the list immediately from whatever is cached, so pages and actions work instantly, before any data arrives.
Remembers which opening this is.
Refreshes the cache (a no-op if it is under 15 seconds old).
If the palette was closed, reopened, or turned into the API-key prompt while the data loaded, the stale list is dropped. It used to render the commands into the key prompt.
Rebuilds the items with the fresh incidents, customers and scenarios and renders again, keeping whatever the user typed in the meantime.
Fades the rows in while sliding them 4px from the left, 8ms apart (`stagger(8)`), a quick ripple down the list.
If loading fails (for example, the server is unreachable) the error is swallowed on purpose: navigation and actions keep working. The last line closes the function.
Doc comment: the palette doubles as the API-key prompt when the server is not running in demo mode (in demo mode the server injects the key into the page).
`askForKey(after)` switches the palette into key mode and stores `after`, the callback to run once a key is saved. main.js calls it when api.js reports a 401 response to a write request.
Mounts a frame with a key-specific placeholder. Because `mode` is now 'key', `frame()` renders the key icon, a password input and the session-only footer.
Replaces the results area with a lock icon and a one-line explanation of why a key is needed.
Shows the palette (which focuses the input) and closes the function.
`closePalette()` is async so the exit animation can be awaited.
Does nothing if the palette is already hidden.
Remembers which opening this close belongs to.
Waits for a quick exit animation: fade out while shrinking to 97%, in 140ms.
If the palette was opened again during those 140ms (say a palette action got a 401 and `askForKey()` showed the key prompt), this close is stale and must not hide the new content.
Otherwise hides the palette and empties it.

Gives focus back to where it was before the palette opened, unless the chosen action moved it on purpose (opening a drawer focuses the drawer). Hiding the focused input leaves focus on the page body, which is how the first case is recognized; focus used to stay on the body.
Closes the function.
`installPalette()` runs once at startup (main.js) and attaches delegated listeners to the permanent `#palette` container.
Keeps Tab and Shift+Tab inside the palette box while it is open (see `trapTab` in dom.js).
Clicks: anything marked `data-close` (the backdrop) closes the palette.
Clicking a result looks up its item through `data-i` in `filtered`, closes the palette and runs the item's action. The close isn't awaited, so the action starts while the exit animation plays.
Closes the click listener.
Typing in command mode resets the highlight to the first row and re-filters the list. In key mode typing triggers nothing.
Keyboard handling: Escape always closes the palette, and `preventDefault` keeps the browser from also acting on the key.
In key mode, Enter with a non-empty value saves the key (`setKey` trims it and stores it in `sessionStorage`), closes the palette, confirms with a toast and runs the `onKey` callback.
Returns early so the list-navigation keys below never run in key mode; then closes the `if`.
Arrow Up and Down move the highlight; `preventDefault` stops the text cursor from jumping to the start or end of the input.

Moves the index by one with wrap-around. Adding `filtered.length` before `%` keeps the result non-negative when going up from row 0, and `Math.max(..., 1)` avoids taking a remainder by zero when there are no results.
Updates the highlight and scroll position without re-rendering the list.
Otherwise, if Enter is pressed while a result is highlighted, the key press is claimed with `preventDefault`.
Takes the highlighted item, closes the palette and runs its action, exactly like clicking it.
Closes the `else if`, the keydown listener and `installPalette()`.
